steps.what: Follow principles of radiation protection for patient, self and others during actual work

tasks.design: Keep radiation-protection conduct and checks with the therapist. Existing protective equipment and interlocks remain part of actual work; their runtime is not a new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protection requires actual safe conduct around the patient and treatment environment.
tasks.enabler_now: No justified labour-reducing change within the stated conduct task.
tasks.still_hard: Patient condition, room occupancy and safe practice require actual observation.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist acts on the real situation rather than assuming a completed electronic field proves safety.
tasks.altitude: No proposed reduction in protection work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: radiation protection involves actual protective conduct; digital completion alone does not establish safe conditions.

assumptions: Boundary is following protection principles during actual work. No separate record write, report, digital send or equipment-setting transaction is specified here; actual such duties must be decomposed separately rather than hidden in physical work.
Existing interlocks and protective equipment earn zero new saving. The full share is provisional, not a measured baseline; protection checks remain fully retained.
No software change is introduced, so no incremental upkeep arises.
unknowns: Does this local task include a distinct protection record?
research_questions: Observe actual conduct and any separate documentation before proposing a change.

incremental.description: No software introduced; no incremental upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All actual protection conduct remains retained; gross saving and new work are zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review prescriptions, diagnosis, charts and patient identification.

steps.what: Retrieve actual prescription, diagnosis and patient chart in the oncology information system {OTHER}
Review prescription, diagnosis, patient chart and actual patient identification
outputs: actual patient and prescription review findings

tasks.design: Configure native linked prescription and chart views in the oncology information system {OTHER}. The therapist still reviews the actual content and confirms patient identification directly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review can require navigating separate source views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient-context links can reduce navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Identity, clinical consistency and prescription interpretation require actual review.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist detects contradictions between the patient, prescription and treatment context.
tasks.altitude: Less source navigation; clinical review stays intact.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native oncology information views can link prescription and chart sources; they do not replace actual patient identification or clinical review.

assumptions: Actual authorised prescription and patient chart already exist; source owners supply correct patient and version identifiers. Therapist verifies linkage in s1 and reads/interprets content and checks actual identity in s2; missing records remain manual.
Only repeated navigation is eligible. No clinical review or patient-identity check is removed. Existing linked views earn zero saving.
Boundary is review, with no separate record write, report, send or treatment-setting action specified; actual additional transactions must be separated and measured.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native configuration first, no model required.
unknowns: Are sources already in one patient view?
How much effort is navigation rather than clinical review?
research_questions: Can native source links shorten navigation without weakening version and identity checks?

incremental.description: Check patient-context source links and version display.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.40 navigation = 8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 7.5. Half eligible gives 4 minus 0.5 = 3.5. All actual clinical and identity review stays retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter prescribed data and set treatment-equipment controls.

steps.what: Verify actual authorised prescription and patient-specific equipment-setting source fields
Enter data into computer from verified actual prescribed setting fields
Check exact final patient-specific settings, dose units, equipment and authorised prescription
outputs: checked final prescribed setting packet and exact target equipment

steps.what: Commit the checked final prescribed setting packet to the treatment record
inputs: checked final prescribed setting packet and exact target equipment

steps.what: Set controls to operate or adjust equipment or regulate prescribed dosage
inputs: checked final prescribed setting packet and exact target equipment

tasks.design: Use only supported native prescribed-field transfer from the oncology information system {OTHER} to the treatment equipment system {OPS_SYSTEM}. The therapist verifies the source, checks the complete final setting packet, commits it and personally sets equipment controls under actual treatment procedures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prescribed fields may be retyped between already digital treatment systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported native field mappings can reduce exact transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Correct patient, dose, units, machine state and actual treatment authority require full checks.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist detects a technically valid transfer that does not match the actual patient or authorised treatment.
tasks.altitude: Less exact prescribed-field entry; no autonomous dose choice or equipment operation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supported treatment-system interfaces can transfer prescribed fields; local support and validation must be established, and no dose decision is delegated.

assumptions: Actual authorised treatment-planning owner supplies patient identifier, exact plan version, prescribed settings and units, and target equipment. Therapist verifies all source fields in s1; unsupported or ambiguous fields remain manual in s2.
Only exact re-entry into a draft is eligible. All existing identity, prescription, setting and equipment checks remain retained; no clinical validation is replaced by a technical import check.

Equipment-setting action is separately gated on the final exact setting packet after it exists. Treatment delivery and any independent dose change are outside this entry/setup boundary and require actual clinical authority; no avoided labour is claimed.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native supported integration first; already automatic transfer and interface runtime earn zero saving. Routine record commit retains one percent and uses the existing final setting check.
unknowns: Which prescribed fields are actually retyped?
Is a supported native draft-transfer interface available?
research_questions: Can verified exact-field transfer reduce entry while preserving every actual treatment check?

incremental.description: Check supported field mappings, units and plan-version behaviour after system changes.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final prescribed setting packet and exact patient record destination; edits require recheck
s3 exact final prescribed setting packet, patient and target equipment; any setting or target change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 30*0.50 exact-field entry = 15; minus 1 upkeep = 14. Half eligible gives 7.5 minus 1 = 6.5. Source checks, final checks, record commit and physical control setting remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe patients, reassure them and respond to adverse reactions.

steps.what: Observe patients during actual radiation treatment for unusual reactions
Reassure patients during treatment and hear their actual concerns
Recognise adverse reactions and determine the immediate required equipment response
outputs: actual immediate stop decision for exact operating equipment when required

steps.what: Turn equipment off immediately when an unexpected adverse reaction requires stopping
inputs: actual immediate stop decision for exact operating equipment when required

steps.what: Prepare and check actual unusual-reaction report and physician recipient
inputs: actual physician recipient and patient reference
outputs: checked final unusual-reaction report and exact physician recipient

steps.what: Report actual unusual reactions to the physician using the checked final report
inputs: checked final unusual-reaction report and exact physician recipient

tasks.design: Configure existing patient-reference fields in the oncology information system {OTHER} for actual reaction reports. Observation, reassurance and immediate stop decisions remain fully human; the therapist stops equipment when required and checks actual report content before its separate delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: An existing reaction report can repeat patient and treatment references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient-context fields can reduce exact reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising adverse reactions and responding immediately require direct clinical attention.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist notices changes, reassures the patient and acts on the actual situation.
tasks.altitude: Less existing reaction-report reference entry; patient attention and response remain intact.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native patient-context report fields can reduce duplicate references; they do not recognise reactions, decide treatment response or establish that a stop occurred.

assumptions: Therapist supplies actual symptoms, timing and actions in retained s5; native record supplies only actual patient/treatment references. Missing data stays manual. No free audio capture or automatic clinical narrative is assumed.

Observation, reassurance, reporting and stopping are conditional task branches, not mandatory events in every treatment. Shares are provisional, not measured baselines; reweight actual oral-only reports and no-reaction cases. No artificial digital record is required.
The stop gate is the therapist's immediate actual decision for exact equipment under existing procedure, adding no approval step or delay. Equipment stop is never inferred from the decision alone.

Existing structured report defaults earn zero saving. S6 is the single actual report delivery/commit; any extra actual record save must be separately counted. Routine delivery retains one percent and uses s5's existing content check.
unknowns: Are reaction reports actually entered digitally?
research_questions: Can native report context reduce duplicate entry without delaying patient response?

incremental.description: Maintain actual patient-reference and recipient defaults.

approvals.approved_version: s3 actual immediate stop decision for exact operating equipment; changed equipment requires actual reassessment without added delay
s5 checked final actual unusual-reaction report and exact physician recipient; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 18*0.20 repeated report references = 3.6; minus 0.5 upkeep = 3.1. Half eligible gives 1.8 minus 0.5 = 1.3. All patient observation, reassurance, clinical decisions, stop and report delivery remain retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Therapists retain clinical checks, protection, patient attention and actual equipment authority; only demonstrated repeated navigation and entry may shrink.
skills_to_grow: Exact source and target version checks
